title: Power Automate: generate documents from SharePoint document generation forms
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licence prerequisites, preview qualifications and data policy control are supported. Minor corrections would complete the form-creation route and acknowledge that the checklist's permission and licence reviews have no corresponding controls-table rows.

claims.claim: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping flow input data to document generation template fields.
claims.quote: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to a document generation template and saves the output to a SharePoint library.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The action saves generated documents to a SharePoint library.
claims.quote: Generate document from form (Preview) creates documents by mapping input data to a document generation template and saves the output to a SharePoint library.

claims.claim: The source template must be a Microsoft Word document in .docx format.
claims.quote: The source document must be a Microsoft Word document (.docx format).

claims.claim: The roadmap says the action returns the generated document with file metadata such as location and status.
claims.quote: The action works by mapping input data to template fields and returns the generated document along with file metadata such as location and status.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives contracts, invoices, letters and reports as example uses.
claims.quote: This capability supports scenarios such as creating contracts, invoices, letters, or reports using structured templates and form-driven inputs.

claims.claim: A content manager starts turning a Word template into a form through the Forms command in a SharePoint document library.
claims.quote: In a SharePoint document library, select Forms from the command bar. Select Document generation form to start the form creation process.
claims.fix: Complete the sentence's route as 'Forms > Document generation form' in a SharePoint document library, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/copilot-in-sharepoint-structured-document-generation.

claims.where: controls[0].governs, scope and note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern which connectors flows in the policy's environments may combine with the SharePoint connector, which contains this action.
claims.quote: By moving the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors to the Business data group, you're preventing users from creating flows and apps that combine these two connectors with any of the connectors in the Non-business or Blocked groups.

claims.claim: SharePoint is not blockable through the data policy Block action, although it can be placed in a data group.
claims.quote: For connectors like SharePoint that aren't blockable, the Block action isn't available and a warning appears.

claims.claim: Following the tenant-level data policy steps requires the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Following the environment-level data policy steps requires Power Apps Environment Admin permissions, except for the separately stated Dataverse case.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: For environments with a Dataverse database, the environment-level policy administrator needs the System Administrator role instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center route Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > + New Policy > Pre-built connectors > SharePoint > Move to Business places SharePoint in Business.
claims.quote: Select Security ... under Settings, select Data and privacy ... Data policy ... + New Policy ... In the Pre-built connectors page ... select the Salesforce and SharePoint connectors, and then select Move to Business from the top menu bar.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy -PolicyName <policy GUID> -Classification Confidential -Connectors <connector objects> moves the supplied connectors to the policy's Business group.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively). ... The policy name (GUID). ... If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: The governance checklist's permission and licence controls are represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review Edit permissions ... Check which Microsoft Copilot licences are assigned ... Review the destination libraries for who can open the generated documents. The sole controls-table row governs connector combinations.
claims.fix: The Before rollout steps to review library Edit permissions and Copilot licence assignments, and the After rollout step to review generated-document access, have no corresponding controls-table rows. Do not add rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Nothing is documented that changes what users outside the maker, content-manager and form-submitter roles see.
claims.quote: Searched: document generation forms default; SharePoint document generation forms Power Automate admin enable disable tenant site default rollout Set-SPOTenant. Read roadmap, generation page and connector article; no change to other users' existing experience was stated.
